deities: Nature and earth deities (Mishmi indigenous faith)

history.summary: NOT A BUDDHIST TEMPLE AND NOT A TEMPLE AT ALL — keep-or-drop/reclassification decision needed. Tamla-Du is the annual festival of the Mishmi (Digaru Mishmi) community, celebrated on 15 February at a festival ground in Tezu, Lohit district, where prayers are offered to the god/nature deities of earth for prosperity and protection (the 56th Central Tamla-Dü Festival was held at Tezu in February 2026). The CSV row's label 'Tamla-Du Buddhist Temple' conflates this Mishmi indigenous-faith festival with a Buddhist temple. Researched here as the Central Tamla-Du festival site; recommend relabelling the row as a festival site, in the same way as other CSV festival entries. Coordinates are approximate Tezu-town coordinates.

name: Tamla-Du Festival Ground, Tezu
town_description: Tezu is the headquarters town of Lohit district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Lohit river at about 185 m elevation. It is the Mishmi community's main town and home to the Dhargyeling Tibetan settlement.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Open ground; active around the 15 February festival
